questions.stem: On the Backups screen **Last backup** is Passed (from 02:00 UTC), but **WAL archive lag** is 4,200 s (Critical, threshold 300 s) and one storage target is Failed. What is the real risk?

options.text: There is no risk, because the 02:00 backup passed.
Recent changes are not safely archived, and unarchived WAL piles up on the database disk until archiving resumes.
Every older backup in the bucket has been deleted.

questions.why: A passed nightly backup says nothing about the last hours. High archive lag means a disaster now would lose more than a few seconds, and the database keeps what it could not deliver.

questions.stem: A restore drill ends Drill failed. Double-entry zero drift and Sharded balance parity show Passed, but Audit hash chain shows Failed. What do you do?

options.text: Ignore it, because the money checks passed.
Delete the audit database so the next drill passes.
Treat it as a priority-1 incident: escalate to the Security Admin, keep every backup and do not alter audit records.

questions.why: A failed audit chain means an audit row may be changed, damaged or missing. Backups are the evidence, so they must be kept.

questions.stem: Why does lowering **Full retention days** need a second Security Admin?

options.text: So one compromised or mistaken account cannot shorten the history that recovery and investigations depend on.
Because cron expressions must be typed by two people at the same time.
Because the backup daemon cannot store retention settings.

questions.why: Policy changes use maker-checker (`BACKUP_POLICY`), and the checker must be a different Security Admin.

questions.stem: What does a restore drill do to the production database?

options.text: It restores the latest backup over production to prove it works.
It pauses production for a few minutes so the checks are exact.
Nothing: it restores into an isolated scratch cluster with archiving switched off, then destroys that cluster.

questions.why: The scratch cluster listens on the loopback address only and cannot write into the real archive, so production is never touched.

questions.stem: You click **Run backup now** while a restore drill is already running. What happens?

options.text: The drill is cancelled and the backup starts at once.
Both run at the same time to save time.
The backup is queued and runs after the drill, in order.

questions.why: Only one backup or drill job runs at a time; extra requests wait in order, and a repeated request with the same Idempotency-Key is not run twice.
